boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along the Main, Oak, Warwick, Rockhill, Cherry, and 43rd Street corridors bordering UMKC’s Volker campus.

cards.title: The Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: Oak Street corridor, near 45th Street
cards.notes: Walk the Oak Street corridor to enter the museum and use its detailed visitor map to choose galleries, accessibility options, or a timed visit.
cards.short_summary: A nearby art museum with free general admission and a substantial permanent collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nelson-Atkins states that visitors can see more than 5,000 years of art for free and provides museum visitor information.
cards.source_title: Plan your visit to The Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Check the museum’s visit page for current daily hours, gallery closures, and entry guidance.

cards.title: Donald J. Hall Sculpture Park
cards.subtitle: Oak Street corridor, south of the Nelson-Atkins
cards.notes: Use the south lawn paths from Oak Street to see the outdoor monumental works, including the shuttlecock sculptures, during daylight.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor sculpture destination beside the Nelson-Atkins campus-facing route.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nelson-Atkins identifies the Donald J. Hall Sculpture Park as free to visit and open from sunrise to sundown.
cards.source_title: Plan your visit to The Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access is listed as sunrise to sundown; follow museum grounds rules.

cards.title: Kemper Museum of Contemporary Art
cards.subtitle: Warwick Boulevard corridor, near 44th Street
cards.notes: Approach on Warwick Boulevard and check the museum’s current exhibition information before going; the venue’s free-access model covers its exhibitions.
cards.short_summary: A contemporary-art museum at 4420 Warwick Boulevard, just north of UMKC’s orbit.
cards.evidence_claim: Kemper Museum’s official 2026 event information states that museum admission is always free and gives its address as 4420 Warwick Boulevard.
cards.source_title: Kemper Museum Gala: Know Before You Go
cards.access_notes: Confirm current gallery hours and exhibition availability with Kemper before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Emily & Todd Voth Artspace at KCAI
cards.title: Emily & Todd Voth Artspace at KCAI
cards.subtitle: 43rd Street corridor at Walnut Street
cards.notes: Follow 43rd Street to the KCAI exhibition space and check its program calendar for current shows, talks, and any visit-specific guidance.
cards.short_summary: A KCAI contemporary-art venue renamed in 2025 and positioned at 16 East 43rd Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Kansas City Art Institute says the Emily & Todd Voth Artspace at 16 East 43rd Street provides free and accessible arts programming.
cards.source_title: KCAI’s Artspace Announces Bold New Era with Renaming to The Emily & Todd Voth Artspace
cards.access_notes: Review current exhibition and event details before arrival.

cards.title: Community Christian Church
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor at 46th Street
cards.notes: Pause along Main Street to view the Frank Lloyd Wright-designed sanctuary, then consult the church schedule if you plan to attend worship or arts programming.
cards.short_summary: A National Register-listed Frank Lloyd Wright building at 4601 Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Community Christian Church says its sanctuary was designed by Frank Lloyd Wright and identifies its location as 4601 Main Street.
cards.source_title: Community Christian Church: Frank Lloyd Wright
cards.access_notes: The building is an active church; use posted service and program information for interior access.

cards.entity_name: Plaza Branch, Kansas City Public Library
cards.title: Plaza Branch
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor at 48th Street
cards.notes: Enter from Main Street to browse, study by the floor-to-ceiling windows, and locate the permanent “Good As Gold” book sculpture in the foyer.
cards.short_summary: A public-library branch at 4801 Main Street with a permanent sculpture made of books.
cards.evidence_claim: Kansas City Public Library lists Plaza Branch at 4801 Main Street and identifies “Good As Gold” as a permanent foyer sculpture there.
cards.source_title: Plaza Branch | Kansas City Public Library
cards.access_notes: The library lists current hours on its location page; visitors should observe library policies.

cards.entity_name: Ewing and Muriel Kauffman Memorial Garden
cards.title: Ewing and Muriel Kauffman Memorial Garden
cards.subtitle: Rockhill Road corridor, near 48th Street
cards.notes: Use the Rockhill Road entrance for a garden walk, then follow posted on-site rules while visiting the memorial landscape and adjoining foundation campus.
cards.short_summary: A memorial garden on the Kauffman Foundation campus at 4801 Rockhill Road.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ewing Marion Kauffman Foundation identifies the Memorial Garden as part of its 4801 Rockhill Road campus and describes it as the final resting place of Ewing and Muriel Kauffman.
cards.source_title: Our Campus | Ewing Marion Kauffman Foundation
cards.access_notes: Check the garden’s current visitor information before making a dedicated trip.

cards.title: Linda Hall Library
cards.subtitle: Cherry Street corridor at 51st Street
cards.notes: Bring photo ID if you want borrowing access, or use the Main Reading Room, study rooms, and public browsing areas during listed library hours.
cards.short_summary: A science, engineering, and technology library at 5109 Cherry Street that welcomes public research visits.
cards.evidence_claim: Linda Hall Library states that it is open to the public free of charge and that its Main Reading Room and study rooms are open to visitors.
cards.access_notes: The library lists public hours as Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; rare-book use requires an appointment.

cards.title: Linda Hall Library Arboretum
cards.subtitle: Cherry Street corridor at 51st Street
cards.notes: Take a grounds walk around the library to see labeled tree diversity and tree peonies; keep pets leashed and leave picnics and hammocks at home.
cards.short_summary: A 14-acre urban arboretum surrounding Linda Hall Library with more than 300 trees.
cards.evidence_claim: Linda Hall Library says its 14-acre arboretum has more than 300 trees and that the grounds are open to the public from 5 a.m. to 11 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Grounds are listed as open 5 a.m.–11 p.m.; comply with the library’s grounds rules.

cards.entity_name: The National Museum of Toys and Miniatures
cards.title: The National Museum of Toys and Miniatures
cards.subtitle: Oak Street corridor at 52nd Street
cards.notes: Use the 52nd Street entrance for the museum lot, reserve tickets if needed, and allow time for the first-floor miniatures and second-floor toy galleries.
cards.short_summary: A two-floor museum at 5235 Oak Street on the southwest corner of the UMKC campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Museum of Toys and Miniatures says it is at 5235 Oak Street, on UMKC’s southwest campus corner, with two floors devoted to miniatures and toys.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | The National Museum of Toys and Miniatures
cards.access_notes: The museum encourages advance ticket reservations because gallery capacity is limited; parking is listed as free.
